I am an old woman of 71 years, and this small plot of less than a tenth of a hectare is all we have here in Dodoma. The land is dry and the rains are not always kind, so I plant what I know will feed us — mixed together as my mother taught me. I have no money for chemical fertilizer or sprays, but I put the manure from our few animals on the soil, and I use the seeds I saved from last harvest. My hands are old but I still work this plot myself; my grandchildren help when they can.
